title: A tokenizer

milestone.title: From Machine Code to Modern Languages

description:
Split a line of code into tokens, the first job of every compiler.

```
total = price * 3 + 10
NAME 'total'  EQUALS  NAME 'price'  STAR  NUMBER 3  PLUS  NUMBER 10
```

starter.main.py:
def tokenize(text):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(text):
        ch = text[i]
        # TODO
        i += 1
    return tokens


print(tokenize("total = price * 3 + 10"))

hints: When `ch.isdigit()`, keep moving `i` forward while the next character is a digit too (lesson 5.03).
A dictionary `{"=": "EQUALS", "+": "PLUS", ...}` handles all the symbols with one lookup.
requirements: Token kinds: `NAME` (letters and `_`), `NUMBER` (digits), and one kind per symbol `= + - * / ( )`.
Skip spaces; an unexpected character prints `unexpected '?' at column n`.
Walk the text with an index, not with `split`.
stretch: Add decimal numbers and two-character operators like `==`.
